title: A New Radio to Overcome Critical Link Budgets

predicted_errors.error_location: Section III.A, Eq. (3) and surrounding text
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines F_b in C^{T x T} and then writes T_b = diag(x_b) F_b as an N x T matrix, while diag(x_b) has dimension N x N (or at most a rectangular N x T diagonal but not as stated). For N != T these dimensions do not multiply. The examples use T=18.375 and T=46 with N=16 or N=32, so the matrix dimensions are inconsistent.

The text says 'If the matrix F_b is unitary' while treating F_b as an N x T matrix with T > N. A rectangular matrix with orthogonal rows is not unitary; unitarity requires a square matrix. The paper's later examples have T != N, so the term 'unitary' is mathematically wrong.

predicted_errors.error_location: Numerical example with N=32 antennas, T=46, second narrower-spectrum example
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states 'The combining gain is 15 dB, exactly the same as for transmit beamforming.' For a temporal combining factor T=46, the expected combining gain is 10 log10(46) = 16.6 dB, not 15 dB. Transmit beamforming with N=32 gives 10 log10(32) = 15.05 dB. This also contradicts the earlier statement that temporal combining gain can exceed beamforming gain when T > N.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract versus receiver description in Section IV
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract says common proposals rely on analog beamforming at both transmitter and receiver, whereas MA-TISK 'does not require beam alignment.' However, the receiver section says the receiver employs 'analog beamforming towards the transmitter.' Analog beamforming inherently requires beam/channel alignment, so this contradicts the abstract's no-beam-alignment claim.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section IV, numerical example describing the leftmost subcarrier transition
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: In the phase-transition discussion, the paper says that for the leftmost subcarrier a frequency deviation toward lower frequencies creates out-of-band radiation and should be avoided, whereas for the rightmost subcarrier lowering is in-band. But the numerical example says: 'The four possible symbol transitions for the leftmost subcarrier are shown in Fig. 2 ... The phase is changed by temporarily lowering the frequency.' For the leftmost/lowest-frequency subcarrier this violates the paper's own design rule; it should raise the instantaneous frequency toward the band center.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section IV numerical examples, 'we set T = 18.375'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: T is used as a matrix/vector dimension in Eq. (3)-(6), e.g., F_b in C^{T x T} and f_{b,n}^{(S)} in C^{1 x ST}, with integer sample indices running to ST-1. Setting T=18.375 gives a fractional number of samples/columns, which is not a valid discrete sequence length unless a specific non-integer oversampling convention is introduced. The paper does not provide such a convention.

The paper states MA-TISK 'does not suffer from spectral re-growth issues plaguing other constant envelope modulations like GMSK.' GMSK is a constant-envelope modulation specifically designed for tight spectral containment and does not exhibit spectral regrowth under nonlinear amplification. Characterizing GMSK as plagued by spectral regrowth is misleading.
